page_title: Push Notifications on the Web (Building a PWA, Part 3)

summary.title: Push Notifications on the Web (Building a PWA, Part 3)
summary.one_liner: You learn how to add client-side web push notifications using the Push API, a Service Worker, and Firebase Cloud Messaging, including subscribing, unsubscribing, and triggering weekly sends.
keywords: how to send push notifications to users
takeaways: Push subscriptions are created through the Service Worker's pushManager, so a registered, active Service Worker is required first.
Call pushManager.subscribe({userVisibleOnly: true}) and send the subscription endpoint ID to your server to store it.
Unsubscribing takes two steps: call getSubscription() then unsubscribe(), and delete the stored ID from the database.
Firebase Cloud Messaging needs the Sender ID in manifest.json; the Server Key is used by the server when posting messages.
Weekly sends were triggered by an IFTTT recipe POSTing to the backend endpoint, rather than running the script manually.
summary.summary: The author, building a PWA for their blog, explains the client side of web push notifications. The article covers how the Push API works together with a Service Worker and Firebase Cloud Messaging, with the server side handled by a separate Rails app written by a collaborator. Code snippets show registering the Service Worker, subscribing users, saving the subscription ID via an API, unsubscribing and deleting that ID, and triggering weekly notifications through an IFTTT recipe. It ends with a note linking to caniuse.com for browser support of the Push API.
